newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Violence escalates at Israel-Lebanon border.
newsitem.headline: Violence escalates at Israel-Lebanon border.

text.p: Violence flared at the Israel-Lebanon border overnight. Hizbollah guerrillas set off a roadside bomb and fired mortar rounds. Israeli forces retaliated with an air attack.
Israeli army officials said on Thursday that a pro-Israeli militiaman and an Arab guerrilla were killed.
The bomb exploded late on Wednesday in the Jezzine area of south Lebanon just outside Israel's occupation zone, military sources said.
It killed a pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiaman and lightly wounded three, the sources said.

In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) claimed responsibility for the roadside bomb. SLA sources said the explosion prompted retaliatory Israeli shelling north of Jezzine in south Lebanon.

Israel's army said its troops killed the guerrilla and wounded others in fighting in the eastern sector of the occupation zone. The army said its warplanes also struck a guerrilla target in southern Lebanon.

The mortar rounds fired from Lebanon exploded on both sides of the border before dawn on Thursday, injuring no one, the army said. Military sources said the rounds were apparently aimed at troops and not northern Israeli residents.
Israel's northern commander Major-General Amiram Levine said Hizbollah fired the 120-mm mortars along with Katyusha rockets which did not slam into the Israeli side.
Levine told reporters Hizbollah was feeling pressured having suffered casualties in more than five clashes with Israeli troops in the last week.
"We have no intention of escalating the situation. We aren't firing at our initiative into Lebanese villages and we have no interest in fighting in the settlements, next to the settlements," he said.

"But if Hizbollah fires at posts, fires next to our communities and it does that next to the Lebanese communities, it brings the war itself into the Lebanese communities and for self-defence the Israeli army and SLA will have to respond."

The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine-mile)-deep zone in south Lebanon to guard northern Israel from guerrilla attacks. Hizbollah aims to drive the Israelis out.
The rise in tensions on Israel's northern front followed a day of Israeli-Palestinian unrest in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Israeli troops, coming under a rain of petrol bombs and rocks, fired rubber-coated metal bullets and wounded 37 Palestinians in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said. Soldiers shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza.
Israel warned the Palestinian Authority to quell the violence or risk a stronger military response.
